name: Lovable
summary: AI app builder that turns a written description into a web app with a database and hosting, published to a lovable.app address in one click. Billing is in credits whose cost per message depends on the work, and a published app's backend runs on a separate monthly Cloud allowance.
best_for: founders, marketers and small teams who want a working web app with a database from a written description, online the same day without setting up hosting
skip_if: your app must keep saving data all month on a zero budget, or your team wants to write and review the code itself rather than prompt for changes
honest_knock: You do not know what a change costs until it is done. Lovable prices each build message by the work it turns out to involve, from about half a credit for a styling tweak to two credits for a page with images, so a credit budget is an estimate, not a price list. The second catch is easy to miss: the app you publish runs its database, hosting and AI features on a separate monthly Cloud grant of 20 credits. Lovable's own documentation says a published app stays live when those credits run out, but its backend services and AI features pause, so an app that works on day one can stop saving data later in the month. The larger Pro tiers are no cheaper per credit until 1,200 credits a month, so buying ahead saves nothing below that.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-26 on lovable.dev/pricing from a European exit, so shown in euros including VAT, and in Lovable's plans-and-credits documentation) Free: 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month, which do not roll over; plus a monthly Cloud grant of 20 credits for hosting and backend services and 4 credits for AI features inside published apps. Pro starts at 25 euros a month for 100 credits, with a dropdown of larger credit tiers: 200 for 50 euros, 400 for 100 euros and 800 for 200 euros keep the same 25 cents a credit, and the discounts only start at 1,200 credits for 294 euros (2%), rising to 10% at 5,000 credits for 1,125 euros. Pro adds custom domains, removing the Lovable badge, credit rollover for one month, on-demand top-ups and user roles. Business starts at 50 euros a month for the same 100 credits and adds SSO, a security center, internal-only publishing and personal projects. Enterprise is a platform fee on volume pricing. Yearly billing is advertised as two months free. What a message costs depends on the work: the documentation gives about 0.50 credits for a styling change, 1.20 for adding authentication and 2.00 for a landing page with images, and Plan mode costs 1 credit a message.

structured_checks.task: Code can be exported (GitHub or zip) and data downloaded
structured_checks.detail: run on 26 September 2026: GitHub connected with access limited to one repository; Lovable created its own repository holding the full source and the database migrations, with no secret keys committed. Outside Lovable (Node 22) the code installed and built without errors, and the dev server showed the page but loaded no classes, because the database service key and admin password stay in Lovable. Data leaves as the admin CSV (T14) or Lovable's full database export (documented, not triggered).
structured_checks.applies_to: the product as it was on run_date, on the plan stated; a later version inherits nothing

sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt. Lovable paid us nothing when we ran the test; it accepted us into its affiliate programme on 28 September 2026, and these findings were recorded before that.
findings: Lovable built and published the app in about ten minutes and used 4 of the 10 credits on a new account. It asked twice, to create the project and to publish, and published to a lovable.app address that stays online on the free plan with an 'Edit with Lovable' badge.

It was the only one of the three whose first version held the limit when ten people booked an eight-spot class at the same moment: eight accepted, two refused with 'Sorry, this class is full.' The other two accepted all ten.

It checked input on the server as well as in the form (a name of only spaces and a bad email were refused), kept the admin password out of the page and scripts, and prefixed CSV values starting with = + - or @ so a spreadsheet does not run them as formulas.
It needed no repair round. After republishing, every test booking was still there.

Taking the code with you works, taking the running app does not. With GitHub connected (access limited to one repository), Lovable created its own repository with the full source and database migrations and committed no secret keys. Outside Lovable, on Node 22, it installed and built without errors, but loaded no classes: the database service key and admin password stay in Lovable, so moving means setting up your own database and bringing the bookings as a CSV or Lovable's full database export.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day on the free plan. Not a security audit or a load test, we did not measure how fast the 20 monthly Cloud credits run down, and we did not trigger Lovable's full database export.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
